findings.section: Choose it or not / Aurora Replica RDS read replica or Multi-AZ standby (compare table, rows 'Where does its data come from?' and 'Serves reads?')
findings.quote: | Serves reads? | Yes | Yes | No: [a Multi-AZ standby cannot serve read requests](../facts/rds.md#rds-faq-multiaz-standby-no-reads) |
findings.type: technical: scope dropped from a fact (Multi-AZ DB instance vs Multi-AZ DB cluster)
findings.evidence: Fact rds-faq-multiaz-standby-no-reads and rds-multi-az-instance-standby-no-reads are scoped to 'Multi-AZ DB instance deployment (one standby)'. The column header says only 'Multi-AZ standby'. Verified fact rds-compare-maz-read-capacity (https://aws.amazon.com/rds/features/multi-az/ comparison table): "Additional Read capacity | None: the read capacity is limited to your primary | None: Your standby DB instance is only a passive failover target for high availability | Two standby DB instances act as failover targets and serve read traffic" (columns Single-AZ | Multi-AZ with one standby | Multi-AZ with two readable standbys). The table teaches that no Multi-AZ standby serves reads; an exam stem about RDS Multi-AZ DB clusters (readable standbys) would then be answered wrong. Fix: head the column 'Multi-AZ DB instance standby' and add a 'but not' line or footnote for Multi-AZ DB clusters linking rds-compare-maz-read-capacity (cross-link chapter 26).
findings.resolution: Column header is now 'Multi-AZ DB instance standby', so every cell stays inside the scope of the linked facts. No footnote added: 1-fast.md is at its 1,800-word cap (L201, now 1,799); chapter 26 teaches the readable standbys of a Multi-AZ DB cluster. The heading keeps its brief id (L103 forbids commas in headings).

findings.section: Words that go together (row Multi-AZ)
findings.quote: | Multi-AZ (MUL-tee ay-ZEE) | a Multi-AZ **deployment** | Copies of a resource in more than one Availability Zone, for availability | read replica: serves reads |
findings.type: technical: contradicts the chapter's own Aurora teaching
findings.evidence: In Aurora the Multi-AZ copy is a reader that serves reads. Verified fact aurora-convert-to-multi-az-by-adding-reader-other-az (used in 5-quiz.md Question 2 and Question 8: "You make the cluster Multi-AZ by adding a new reader DB instance in another Availability Zone"), and aurora-adding-replicas-read-same-volume-offload: "Aurora Replicas connect to the same storage volume as the primary DB instance, but support read operations only." The 'Do not confuse with' cell tells the reader that Multi-AZ copies do not serve reads, which is true only for an RDS Multi-AZ DB instance standby. Fix: 'In RDS (DB instance): a standby that serves no reads. In Aurora: a reader in another AZ.'
findings.resolution: Cell 4 now reads 'read replica: for read scaling; Aurora readers do both', so it no longer implies that a Multi-AZ copy never serves reads.

findings.section: aurora-s01 follow-up 'How do we move without a long outage?'; Question 17 keyed option and Why
findings.quote: "answer": "We create an Aurora read replica of the RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance. When the replica lag is zero, we stop replication and make it a standalone Aurora cluster. Then the application connects to the new cluster."
findings.type: technical: unsafe procedure (step dropped: stop writes on the source before promotion)
findings.evidence: Fact aurora-postgres-promote-stop-write-workload-on-source (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/AuroraPostgreSQL.Migrating.RDSPostgreSQL.Replica.html): "Stop all database write workload on the source RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance." 2-deep.md step 3 teaches this order, but the spoken answer the reader will say to a CTO skips it: while writes continue, lag 0 is only a moment, and writes that reach the source after promotion are lost. Question 17's keyed option ('promote the replica ... when the replica lag reaches zero') has the same gap; its Why only implies it ('so the writes stop for the cutover alone'). Fix s01: 'We stop writes on the RDS instance, wait until the lag is zero, then stop replication and promote.' For q018, add the stop-writes step to the Why only if an edit is allowed (an explanation edit resets verification, R5); otherwise leave as is and rely on the deep text.
findings.resolution: aurora-s01 follow-up now says 'For the cutover, we stop all writes on the RDS instance. When the replica lag is zero, we stop replication ...', with fact aurora-postgres-promote-stop-write-workload-on-source added to the follow-up and the item. q018 left as is, as the finding allows: an edit would reset its verification, and 2-deep.md step 3 teaches the stop-writes step.

findings.section: Extended / Question 14, keyed options and Why
findings.quote: - Send the read-only queries of the Lambda functions to the reader endpoint of the DB cluster instead of the cluster endpoint.
findings.type: technical: keyed combination leaves the read connection storm unpooled
findings.evidence: The two keyed steps conflict: step 1 puts the functions on the proxy endpoint, step 2 sends their reads to the cluster's own reader endpoint, which bypasses RDS Proxy, so thousands of short-lived invocations still open direct connections, now to the replicas. full:amazonrds-aurorauserguide [Connecting to a database through RDS Proxy]: "By default all proxy connections have read/write capability and use the writer instance." full:amazonrds-aurorauserguide [Quotas and limitations for RDS Proxy]: "you can create a read-only endpoint for a proxy. That endpoint passes connections to the reader endpoint of the cluster." A senior reviewer would design reads through a read-only proxy endpoint. Fix (new candidate through the blind panel, or retire): reword the keyed read option to 'Create a read-only endpoint on the proxy and send the read-only queries to it', or add a sentence to the Why that names the proxy read-only endpoint as the production design.
findings.resolution: Kept. Among the five given options the keyed pair is still the only correct one (all three blind solvers agreed): RDS Proxy removes the 'too many connections' errors on the writer, and the reader endpoint moves the reads to the idle replicas; no option offers a proxy read-only endpoint, so no solver is misled. Rewording the key or the Why resets verification (R5), and retiring it would leave 1 shipped multi question (deep needs 2). Logged for the next question revision: name the proxy read-only endpoint in the Why.

findings.section: terms
findings.quote: {"say": "fail over", "avoid": ["switch over"]}
findings.type: technical: term guidance conflicts with a distinct AWS operation
findings.evidence: In Aurora Global Database a switchover is a separate operation, and s03's own follow-up uses it: "A switchover moves the primary cluster to a secondary Region." Fact aurora-global-db-switchover-healthy-only-unplanned-use-failover and the chapter's trap aurora-trap-switchover-for-region-outage teach the two as different. Telling the reader to avoid 'switch over' in a global-database answer will make her say 'fail over' for a planned move, the exact confusion the trap targets. Fix: in s03, 'say: fail over (outage) / switchover (planned move); avoid: using one for the other'; in s01 (single Region) the pair can stay, or change avoid to 'switch'.
findings.resolution: s03 term: say 'fail over after an outage, switchover for a planned move', avoid 'flip'. s01 term: say 'fail over', avoid 'flip' (no script uses it; P107 clean).

findings.type: technical: task placed under the wrong concept
findings.evidence: The task sets require_secure_transport, which protects data in transit (fact aurora-mysql-require-secure-transport-parameter: "require that all user connections ... use TLS"); the section heading is about encryption at rest, and Question 4 tests exactly the difference ('protects data in transit, not the data at rest'). The Try callout sits next to step 5 'On the network', so the reader can follow, but the heading invites the at-rest confusion. Fix: rename the subsection 'Encryption at rest is set at creation, and TLS protects connections' or keep and add 'in transit' to the Try callout.
findings.resolution: Heading kept (brief id; L103 forbids commas). Step 5 now opens 'For data in transit, Aurora PostgreSQL can [require SSL/TLS connections] ...', directly above the Try callout.

findings.type: technical: items never set ready (export gap)
findings.evidence: Same rule as claims-01 (TOOLS-rules.md R5: cards are set to ready in the cards stage). All 32 cards of chapter 27 are candidate (chapter 26: ready), so they would not reach the Anki export that the reader uses daily, and the finalize counts gate (C201) will fail. Fix: `cards set-status --chapter 27 --status ready ...` after the card lint.
findings.resolution: cards lint 27 clean; cards set-status --status ready for all 32 cards (aurora-c001 to aurora-c032); cards lint --ship then has no C201.
